kayokyoku.album: Uta wa Waga Inochi (My Song Is My Life)
kayokyoku.note: An overwhelming vocal performance and a gateway to the richness of Shōwa-era kayokyoku. A vocal presence that transcends its era.

folk-newmusic.note: The crystallization of the attempt to set Japanese language to rock rhythm. Its influence on everything that followed is immeasurable.
A landmark of singer-songwriter history, painting personal scenery with vivid harmony and recording.

city-pop.note: Transforms jazz and funk into delicate Japanese-language pop. A rediscovered masterpiece of urban music.
Meticulous chorus work and driving rhythm vividly bind together the images of summer and the city.

technopop.note: The definitive work that turned electronic sound from a futuristic experiment into worldwide pop.
Renewed technopop and idol expression, a defining work of 2000s electronic pop.

idol.note: A masterpiece of idol pop heard as an album, where highly crafted songwriting meets a true star's voice.

rock.note: A debut where simple words and raw impulse connect directly. A timeless gateway into Japanese-language punk.
Brought guitar pop to a wide audience through witty wordplay and crystal-clear melody.

visual-kei.note: Brilliant melody and a versatile band sound coexist with remarkable density.

dance-rnb.note: Fused the physical feel of R&B with natural Japanese lyrics, dramatically shifting the standard for J-POP.
A symbol of the '90s where dance, fashion, and voice connected directly with the spirit of the era.

shibuya-kei.note: A transitional work that broke rock's conventional forms to vividly document the city and everyday life.

internet.note: Connected internet-born sensibility with popular melody, pointing to a new center of gravity.
A work where the design of turning stories into music merges with the speed of the streaming era.

modern-pop.note: Boldly crosses rock, soul, and classical, expanding the image of what a modern band can be.
A light, distinctive debut where piano, soul, and his native Okayama dialect coexist naturally.

japanese-blues.note: Osaka's everyday language, Mitsuteru Kimura's voice, and Kantaro Uchida's guitar crystallize into the starting point of Japanese-language blues.

japanese-blues.artist: Masaki Ueda and South to South
japanese-blues.album: Kono Atsui Tamashii wo Tsutaetainya (I Want to Convey This Burning Soul)
japanese-blues.note: A key work in the history of Kansai Black music, turning the heat of soul and blues into song sung in Kansai dialect.
A defining record of Kansai blues, carved with reverence for Chicago blues and the momentum of young musicianship.

japanese-blues.album: Maki Asakawa no Sekai (The World of Maki Asakawa)
japanese-blues.note: An overwhelming dark texture and Japanese-language expression where jazz, blues, and underground culture intersect.
Delivers the pleasure of jump blues and Japanese-language humor through sharp, large-ensemble playing.

japanese-folk.note: An important early work that carved a sharp social gaze into Japanese-language folk.
Brought personal words and melody to a mass audience, opening the era of the singer-songwriter.
Opened the door from folk to New Music with ambiguous lyrics and vivid sound.
A taut voice and poetry push the expressive limits of folk to their extreme.
Depicts loneliness and homeland in a deep voice, conveying the shadowed emotion of '70s folk.

ska.note: Refines dub space and ska rhythm into a landmark Japanese work that was ahead of the world.
A debut that opened Japanese ska to a wide audience through festive spirit and top-tier musicianship.
Linked the spirit of P.M.A. with high-speed ska punk, connecting the Japanese and American scenes.
A landmark of Japanese ska where deep respect for its roots coexists with Osaka's energy.
Updated ska, calypso, and soul into modern instrumental dance music.
